measured_on.words: Measured on this box, a Windows workstation (dell2) with its local Python 3.14 install of boto3, pandas and pyarrow, reaching S3 over the workstation's ordinary network path to the us-east-1 endpoint; the path itself was not characterised. INFERENCE, not a measurement: a Lambda in us-east-1 reads the same prefixes over the in-region network, so I expect the Lambda to be FASTER on the S3 reads; the build is CPU work whose Lambda speed depends on the function's memory allocation, which was not measured here.

words: Measured LOCAL and read-only: the reporting-gold handler's own filled_inputs and filled_day_rows for the 49 Financial filled_report_values stage, with nothing written and upload never called. The population is the account set run() derives for its newest landed returns day 2026-10-13: population_accounts (the holdings population of the newest holdings partition, 7640 accounts) unioned with newest_accounts (the accounts of the newest account_return_daily partition, 6935 accounts); the union adds no account, so 7640 accounts. filled_inputs read every partition of the returns, activity, realized-lot and class tables, the newest unrealized-lot partition, the served model series and the household crosswalk in 85.295 seconds through 600 S3 requests (590 GET, 10 LIST). filled_day_rows built one day, 2026-10-13: 4012 households and 4693967 rows in 76.283 seconds. The estimate is 85.295 + 10 x 76.283 = 848.12 seconds, over the 600 second line, so the verdict is OWN_INVOCATION. The apply pair must state the 848 second local estimate, its basis (one measured day, ten days per fire, measured locally and not in a Lambda), and that the filled stage runs as its own invocation rather than sharing the 07:41 fire's 900 second timeout.
